related_identifiers.note: Source repository for this deposit. The deposit is the frozen, byte-reproducible archive of the repository at commit 4c2719a; the repository carries full history and continuous integration. Same MIT licence. Neither supersedes the other.

SCOPE NOTE: the AI-consciousness indicator battery exists BOTH as its own deposit and as one investigation (EXP-C001, path 03_INVESTIGATIONS/COMPUTATIONAL_SCIENCE/ai_consciousness_indicators/) inside this laboratory record. Neither supersedes the other; they are the same work at different scopes. Cite the battery deposit when asking about consciousness methodology, and this deposit when asking about the laboratory, its audit trail, or its other 15 experiments. That deposit makes no claim about AI consciousness and scores no AI system. The identifier is v2.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23111535), which corrects v1's mangled references and carries no science that differs from it. Both share concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23101902.

notes: NO PHYSICS DISCOVERY IS CLAIMED. The contribution is evidence about measurement instruments. Four genuine defects were found in the laboratory's own instruments, one of which had previously been counted as a pass. In two of them the defect made the laboratory's own anomaly look SMALLER than it really was. A further nine defects surfaced during publication when the suite was first run on a clean Linux checkout, including a continuous-integration integrity gate that reported success without examining anything -- the same failure mode this deposit documents. Full test suite: 543 passed, 0 failed in the laboratory with complete data. The published tree omits 377 MB of raw simulation output (.npz, .sqlite3), regenerable from seeds recorded in each preregistration; the read-only audit suite reads some of it and fails closed, which is the control working as designed. CI asserts the observed failure set is exactly the recorded excluded-data set, so a new failure fails the build and so does a recorded failure that stops failing. All historical artifacts are verified byte-identical; no baseline control was refreshed. Two preregistrations are labelled informed rather than blind and state what had already been seen.

published_note: Published 2026-10-02. The web form did not carry subjects or references; the deposition API accepts both and silently discards them, so this record has zero of each. Fixing that requires a new version, not an edit.
version_note: Version 2 adds the subjects and references that Zenodo accepted but did not persist in v1. No file, code or scientific content changes: the archive is byte-identical to v1 (md5 21e6429965d9a4943c023e0ddd916bcf, SHA-256 a0750bbc8619e4c807030be1e54a2303b5df2d8b02704d6c76a2995d1cdd0ddf). v1 (10.5281/zenodo.23109117) published with zero subjects and zero references, because Zenodo silently discards both from a deposition-API payload. This version supplies six controlled-vocabulary subject identifiers and six references, each DOI resolved before inclusion. One candidate was rejected during checking: 10.1126/science.1259855 turned out to be Planetary boundaries rather than Ioannidis 2005, whose correct DOI is 10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124.
